name: John Markus Lervik
current_role: Founder, Cognite (Oslo industrial data/AI software); CEO until April 2022, then Chief Strategy & Development Officer
profile: Norwegian tech entrepreneur (b. 1969) with an NTNU PhD. He was CEO of Fast Search & Transfer until Microsoft bought it in 2008, founded ad/analytics firm Cxense in 2010, and in 2016 co-founded Cognite, the Aker-backed industrial DataOps company described as Norway's first unicorn. Girish Rishi took over as CEO in 2022; Cognite now lists Lervik as Founder.
interesting_fact: When he handed over the CEO role in 2022, Cognite's announcement credited him with building Cognite into 'Norway's first unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first person hired at Fast Search & Transfer, and he won an Esso academic award for his NTNU PhD work in 1996. He is a fellow of the Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences.

public_contacts.value: michelle.holford@cognite.com (Michelle Holford, Global PR Lead, Cognite)

notes: Strong fit for the energy/data angle: Cognite does industrial data for oil and gas and utilities. Avoid the 2014 FAST accounting conviction. Cognite now lists him only as 'Founder', so his day-to-day role may be smaller. The PR email was in the media-contact box on a Cognite newsroom page.

name: Pablo Zamora
current_role: President of the board, Fundación Chile (since 2022, proposed by President Boric). Co-founder and former CSO of NotCo. Investor and board member.
profile: Chilean biochemist with a PhD in biotechnology from Universidad de Santiago. In 2015 he co-founded NotCo, the AI-driven plant-based food company later valued as a unicorn, with Matías Muchnick and Karim Pichara. He was CSO from 2018 to March 2020, then left to work as an investor and consultant. He chairs Fundación Chile, whose board is split between the Chilean state and BHP, and was named to BancoEstado's board.
interesting_fact: Fundación Chile's board, which he chairs, is half appointed by the Chilean state and half by the mining company BHP. That gives him a seat where mining, energy and innovation policy meet.
deep_cut_fact: Before NotCo he did postdoctoral research on the genetics of Mexican maize at UC Davis from 2009. He also worked on plant and microbe genomics as a senior scientist with the Mars Advanced Research Institute (2013-2015).
notes: Spanish-language media covers him often (DF, El Mercurio). A 2026 DF piece hinted his Fundación Chile tenure may end with the change of government; I could not confirm his current status. He has spoken publicly about lithium (the SQM-Codelco deal), which fits an energy podcast. No personal email found.

name: Alexander Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder of Marshmallow (London car-insurance insurtech); per 2021 coverage he leads internal culture and product while his twin Oliver handles external matters
profile: British entrepreneur from south-west London who co-founded Marshmallow with his identical twin Oliver and engineer David Goaté. Marshmallow is a licensed UK car insurer that uses data to price cover for people traditional insurers turn away, such as recent migrants and drivers with thin credit files. It became a unicorn in 2021 with an $85M Series B at a $1.25B valuation.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow was only the second UK start-up with Black founders to be valued at more than $1 billion, after WorldRemit.
deep_cut_fact: Marshmallow was first incorporated in 2016 under the name 'Twin Thinking'. For its first 10 months the team worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym on an £80 membership ('a desk plus a sauna and a steam room').
notes: His twin Oliver is the usual press voice, so Alexander gives few interviews. I found no published press email for Marshmallow; the gym anecdote is quoted from Oliver in the Evening Standard (syndicated on Yahoo). I could not verify his current title.

name: Aaron Passey
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Architect, Qumulo (Seattle scale-out file-data platform)
profile: Caltech-trained systems engineer and Isilon Systems veteran who co-founded Qumulo in 2012 with Peter Godman and Neal Fachan and served as its first CTO. He stepped away in 2016, then returned in December 2022 as a senior principal engineer. Qumulo now lists him as Co-founder & Chief Architect; the company sells file storage for AI/GPU, energy and HPC workloads.
interesting_fact: Qumulo's three founders met at Isilon Systems. Passey left Qumulo in 2016 and rejoined in 2022, calling his return 'a true homecoming'.
deep_cut_fact: When he rejoined, Qumulo's CTO Kiran Bhageshpur noted that Passey had worked on four distinct distributed storage products and called him 'a fearless and imaginative technical leader'.
notes: A deeply technical engineer-founder with a low media profile. Good fit for a data-center storage conversation. The best route is Qumulo PR or LinkedIn (linked from Qumulo's leadership page).

name: Amir Jerbi
current_role: Co-founder of Aqua Security; strategic advisor since stepping down as CTO in November 2025
profile: Israeli security engineer who served about four years in an IDF IT unit and later became a chief architect at a large security software company (CA Technologies). In 2015 he co-founded Aqua Security with Dror Davidoff; the cloud-native and container security company reached a $1B valuation in 2021. In November 2025 both founders stepped back to advisory roles, Mike Dube became CEO and Nir Makowski became chief product and technology officer.
interesting_fact: Aqua grew out of a weekly meetup. Jerbi saw an early Docker demo, went home, 'fell in love' with containers within days, and then quit his chief-architect job to work on container security full time.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he decided that 'leveraging containers for better security was my destiny'. He first worked on it as a 'new hobby' before founding Aqua with friends a year later; the original idea was to make containerised apps 'secured anywhere' as well as 'run anywhere'.
notes: The leadership change is dated 5 Nov 2025 (Calcalist). As of 2025, Aqua's press releases appear to route media through an agency (Look Left Marketing), but I could not open the release to verify the address, so it is not recorded. Note that Aqua cut staff after the 2025 reorganisation. He is a technical voice on cloud and container security and appeared on 'The IaC Podcast'.

name: Vu Tran
current_role: Co-founder, Black Sky Industries (Logan, Qld solid-rocket-motor and defence manufacturer); co-founder and former Chief Growth Officer of Go1
profile: Dr Vu Tran is a Brisbane GP who grew up in Logan as a migrant. He co-founded workplace e-learning marketplace Go1 with school friends Andrew Barnes, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; Go1 raised $272M in 2021 and was valued at about $3B when it bought Blinkist in 2023. He has since stepped back from Go1's day-to-day running and co-founded Black Sky Industries, which makes solid rocket propellant and rocket motors for Australian defence.
interesting_fact: Black Sky Industries describes itself as Australia's only sovereign supplier of solid rocket propellant and motors, and it produces ammonium perchlorate locally. Tran argues Australia has only one local firm in the top 100 defence suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: In high school, instead of stacking shelves at Coles, he and Andrew Barnes started a software business that 'made a dollar an hour'. Around 2006 it was building websites for ANZ and News Corp, which did not realise they were dealing with students. He did not pay off his last credit-card debts until early 2020.

public_contacts.value: Long-form interview: 'Meet the Founder - Vu Tran (Go1)', The Exchange by EW Private Wealth, Sept 2024

notes: Practising GP (MBBS Bond, per profiles). Speaks readily on podcasts about sovereign manufacturing and defence, which suits an energy and industry angle. Also a non-executive director of ASX-listed PeopleIN (per marketindex; not re-verified). Black Sky's site has only a contact section, no published email.

name: Justin Waldron
current_role: Co-founder and President, Playco (Tokyo instant-play web games company), per 2020 coverage; current title not re-confirmed
profile: American game developer and angel investor who co-founded Zynga at 19 and was lead engineer/designer on its first game, Texas Hold'em Poker (later Zynga Poker). He rose to SVP Product before leaving in October 2013. He then co-founded Playco in Tokyo with Game Closure's Michael Carter; it raised a $100M Series A in September 2020 at just over $1B, making it a unicorn.
interesting_fact: He was only 19 when he built Zynga Poker, Zynga's first game. On leaving in 2013 he wrote that it had been 'six and a half years since we pushed the button to launch our first game, and each moment since has been magic'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Playco he had invested in more than 50 startups, including Snackpass and Substack. He relocated to Tokyo to run Playco as President.

public_contacts.value: Colossus episode 'Waldron: The Future of Social Gaming'

notes: Lower profile than Zynga co-founder Mark Pincus. Playco's site is still live (games: Everwing, Heads Up!, Buruburu Do Butsu), but I found no post-2021 news on the company's status or his current title. The Colossus podcast page blocked automated access, so I confirmed it only from search results. Several sources say he dropped out of UConn to co-found Zynga.

name: Yu Qianli
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen private-domain operations / creator-commerce SaaS)
profile: One of the ex-Tencent co-founders of Xiaoe-tech, the Shenzhen SaaS company led by founder-CEO Bao Chunjian (鲍春健). Its tools help merchants, educators and creators run e-commerce, marketing and CRM in their own channels. Investors include Tencent, Hillhouse, IDG and Qiming. Its 2021 Series D valued it at about HK$5.1B. It filed for a Hong Kong IPO in August 2025, and 36Kr reported a new attempt in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech's whole founding team came from Tencent. Founder Bao Chunjian left as a rare T4-level expert engineer with ¥5M of savings and burned through it in seven months before the business took off.
deep_cut_fact: 36Kr reports that this co-founder was previously responsible for product development on Tencent's QQ Zone (QQ空间). The article spells the name 喻干里, likely a misprint of 喻千里 (Yu Qianli).
notes: Very low public profile. The only mention I found is in 36Kr, which spells the name 喻干里 rather than 喻千里, so identity is marked uncertain until checked against the HKEX prospectus. Bao Chunjian is the public face and controlling shareholder (about 44.9% pre-IPO). Chinese-language outreach via the company's public-affairs email is the best route.

name: Tjeerd Brenninkmeijer
current_role: Former EVP EMEA / CMO EMEA at Bloomreach (titles from 2019-era author bios); co-founder of Hippo CMS, which Bloomreach acquired in 2016. Current role not confirmed.
profile: Dutch entrepreneur with a Master's in Business Economics from the University of Amsterdam. He co-founded Amsterdam-based Hippo CMS and ran its marketing for 17 years, growing it from three people to a global business of more than 100. After Bloomreach (now a $2B+ commerce/marketing software company) bought Hippo in 2016, he became its CMO and later EVP for EMEA.
interesting_fact: Under his marketing leadership Hippo grew from a three-person start-up to over 100 staff, with subscription revenue up more than 50% a year. Gartner named it a 'visionary' in the Web Content Management Magic Quadrant before the Bloomreach sale.
deep_cut_fact: He has volunteered as a mentor at Startupbootcamp, the European startup accelerator.
notes: Identity is marked uncertain on purpose. He co-founded Hippo, not Bloomreach itself (Raj De Datta and Ashutosh Garg founded Bloomreach), so Hurun's 'BloomReach founder' label is loose. He gets equity through the Hippo acquisition. He is not on Bloomreach's current leadership page, and I found no 2024-26 coverage of him. Dutch business press (MT/Sprout) has interviewed him.

name: Collin Chin
current_role: Co-founder, Aleo (zero-knowledge privacy L1 blockchain); led teams building developer tooling such as the Leo language and Aleo SDK
profile: Collin Chin co-founded Aleo in 2019 with Howard Wu, Raymond Chu and others. Aleo is a programmable privacy blockchain built on zero-knowledge proofs; a16z led its 2021 Series A. At Aleo, Chin worked on the developer stack, especially the Leo programming language for private applications.
interesting_fact: Leo, first released in 2020, was one of the first programming languages built specifically for zero-knowledge applications.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of the 2021 IACR paper 'Leo: A Programming Language for Formally Verified, Zero-Knowledge Applications' (ePrint 2021/651), co-written with Howard Wu, Raymond Chu and formal-methods researchers Alessandro Coglio, Eric McCarthy and Eric Smith.
notes: Low public profile; Howard Wu is Aleo's main public voice. Aleo's author page for him now returns 404, so his current role is unclear. A good angle is the technical depth of the Leo language. I found no personal contact.

name: Jake Benson
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Lukka (New York crypto-asset data and software); left the company in June 2020; current role not found
profile: Jake Benson founded the crypto tax and back-office software vendor Libra in 2014 and rebranded it as Lukka in March 2019 to emphasise crypto data as well as software. Lukka later raised from State Street and S&P Global, and its pricing data underpins S&P Dow Jones crypto indices. Benson left in June 2020, and I found no public record of what he has done since.
interesting_fact: Lukka is named after Luca Pacioli, the 15th-century Franciscan friar who helped popularise double-entry bookkeeping. The 2019 rebrand from 'Libra' was meant to position the company as 'a software and data company for the crypto world'.
deep_cut_fact: Under its original name, Libra, the company raised $25M in two equity rounds. Its December 2020 Series C, led by State Street with S&P Global and CPA.com, was its first equity raise after the rebrand.
notes: He left Lukka in June 2020 (CoinDesk) and has had no public profile since. Lukka's unicorn valuation came after he left. I found no verified current contact; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Guan Dian
current_role: Co-founder, CMO and APAC General Manager, Patsnap (Singapore-founded AI patent and R&D intelligence platform), per Vertex Ventures, Feb 2024
profile: Guan Dian studied management information systems at the National University of Singapore. In 2007 she co-founded Patsnap with fellow NUS student Jeffrey Tiong, starting with a S$50,000 NUS Enterprise grant. Patsnap became a unicorn after a $300M round led by SoftBank and Tencent, and it serves more than 10,000 customers in over 50 countries with AI-powered patent and innovation analytics. She runs marketing and the Asia-Pacific business.
interesting_fact: Patsnap began with a S$50,000 (about US$37,700) grant from NUS Enterprise, and the founders spent two years building their data capabilities before expanding globally.
deep_cut_fact: As an NUS undergraduate she interned in Silicon Valley at a video-streaming company. NUS later gave her its Outstanding Young Alumni Award in 2019.

public_contacts.value: Hard Truths by Vertex, Series 2 Ep 8 (Feb 2024): 'How Guan Dian built a Tech Unicorn from Ground up'

notes: Female co-founder, featured in Vertex's women-founder series. The Vertex episode covers why she left a 'cushy job' to join the startup, a good conversation hook. CEO Jeffrey Tiong is the main press voice. I found no published press email. Her Stanford education appears in some bios but was not verified.

name: Tanmai Gopal
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PromptQL (AI data-agent/AI-native workspace spun out of Hasura); co-founder of Hasura
profile: IIT Madras computer-science graduate who co-founded Hasura with Rajoshi Ghosh. He started as CTO and later became CEO; Hasura's open-source GraphQL Engine has passed 600M downloads and reportedly runs under half the Fortune 500. In 2025 he steered the company into PromptQL, an enterprise AI analyst that raised a $25M Series B and a $100M Series C at a valuation above $1B, and it is now pitched as an AI-native workspace to replace Slack.
interesting_fact: After ChatGPT he concluded his own company was an existential risk and took it through 'three lives in eighteen months': GraphQL engine, AI analyst, then AI workspace. That included moving his team off Slack and living through what he calls three weeks of 'AI psychosis'.
deep_cut_fact: Hasura began as an internal tool. While building a food-delivery venture in Chennai with Rajoshi Ghosh, he wrote a database platform called procrust.es. He also helped create and teach IIT Madras's 'Introduction to Modern Application Development' course.
notes: Very accessible: a frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (The Ken's Zero Shot, July 2026). His X and LinkedIn links come from his AI Engineer speaker page. A strong fit for AI and data-infrastructure conversations.

name: Max M. Diez
current_role: Chairman & Co-Founder, Assaia (Zurich AI/computer-vision platform for aircraft turnarounds); co-founder of Shippo
profile: Zurich-based serial B2B software entrepreneur, listed with Laura Behrens Wu and Simon Kreuz as a 2013 co-founder of Shippo, the San Francisco multi-carrier shipping API later valued at over $1B. He then co-founded Assaia, whose ApronAI uses existing apron cameras to manage aircraft turnarounds in real time for customers such as Alaska Airlines, Southwest and Fraport. He was CEO until January 2024, when he became chairman.
interesting_fact: On handing over Assaia's CEO role in 2024, he predicted that around 80% of airlines and airports would buy turnaround-optimisation technology within a few years, a category Assaia says it created.
deep_cut_fact: Assaia began as computer-vision technology without a use case. Diez and co-founder Nikolay Kobyshev ran workshops to find one, and Swissport's head of innovation saw a demo and said, in effect, 'if this actually worked' it would change apron operations.
notes: Rarely in the press about Shippo, where Laura Behrens Wu is the public face; his early Shippo CTO title appears only in aggregator profiles. Assaia also pitches sustainability benefits (cutting APU use and taxi time), which could interest an energy podcast.

name: Zhoujie Zhou
current_role: Co-founder of Magic Eden (multi-chain crypto/NFT marketplace); listed in profiles as Co-Founder & Chief Engineer
profile: Zhuojie 'Rex' Zhou (Hurun spells it 'Zhoujie') is a Chinese-born engineer who came to the US for graduate school and worked with Sidney Zhang at Uber and Facebook. In 2021 he co-founded Magic Eden with Jack Lu, Sidney Zhang and Zhuoxun Yin; it became Solana's dominant NFT marketplace and a unicorn within months. The company has since gone multi-chain, launched the $ME token, and in 2025 bought the Slingshot trading app.
interesting_fact: The four founders took a week off their day jobs and launched Magic Eden in about eight days to beat a rival 'OpenSea of Solana'. Zhou and Zhang wrote the code. Within weeks it was making US$100,000 a day.
deep_cut_fact: Even with strong revenue, the team raised a US$2.5M seed a month after launch as a 'backstop'. Zhou recalled: 'We were small and paranoid... It's crypto! We didn't know how long the revenue was going to last.' The first six people all worked from six different addresses with no office.
notes: Hurun spells the name 'Zhoujie'; press uses Zhuojie 'Rex' Zhou. He is the most private of the four co-founders; CEO Jack Lu and COO Zedd Yin do the media. I could not verify his current title from a primary source. No personal contact found.

name: Eric Frenkiel
current_role: Co-founder of SingleStore (formerly MemSQL); left in 2017. Reported to have since founded fintech Pomelo (not verified from a primary source).
profile: Stanford engineering graduate who worked on partnership development at Facebook before co-founding MemSQL with Nikita Shamgunov in 2011. MemSQL was a Y Combinator in-memory distributed SQL database backed early by Ashton Kutcher and Max Levchin. He was CEO from the start until 2017. The company was renamed SingleStore, reached a $1.3B valuation, and sold a majority stake to private equity in 2025.
interesting_fact: MemSQL's early backers included Ashton Kutcher, Max Levchin, Aaron Levie and Paul Buchheit. TechCrunch covered the 2012 launch under the headline 'MemSQL Launches With $5M From Ashton Kutcher, Max Levchin & More'.
deep_cut_fact: He was named to Forbes' 30 Under 30 list of technology innovators in both 2011 and 2012, while still in MemSQL's first years.
notes: Low profile since leaving SingleStore in 2017. A secondary blog (Stacksync) says he founded fintech Pomelo, and a Wellfound listing reportedly calls him 'CEO @ Pomelo', but I could not reach Pomelo's site to verify. Treat his current role as unconfirmed. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Byron Nicolaides
current_role: Founder & Group CEO (also styled Chairman & CEO), PeopleCert (global exam/certification body; owner of ITIL/PRINCE2 via Axelos and LanguageCert); former President of CEPIS
profile: Istanbul-born Greek-Turkish entrepreneur and former Merrill Lynch international VP who founded PeopleCert in Athens in 2000. He built it from a Greek player into a global certification group delivering millions of exams in more than 200 countries. Its €450M acquisition of Axelos (ITIL, PRINCE2) was the largest-ever foreign acquisition by Greece's private sector, and PeopleCert calls itself the first Greek-origin unicorn.
interesting_fact: PeopleCert says its €450M Axelos deal was the largest acquisition abroad ever made by the Greek private sector and made PeopleCert the first unicorn of Greek origin.
deep_cut_fact: He holds Greek-Turkish dual citizenship and, per his PeopleCert bio, personally champions CSR projects to safeguard the ancient Greek language. In 2019 he won both European Business Awards UK Entrepreneur of the Year and EY's 'Self-Made' Entrepreneur of the Year in Greece.
notes: Regular speaker at the Delphi Economic Forum, the Thessaloniki Summit and Concordia (New York). I found no published press email. The help-and-support form is customer-oriented; Concordia/Delphi speaker networks may be a warmer route.
